answer: Each season one coastal commons grants exactly one address sole custody of its gale-fed sluice above the tide line, decided by a vote at the mesa and recorded in minutes that neighbouring villages exchange. That grant is the scarce per-head input: a community's decision cannot be printed, and it binds one address to one commons, so no sibling head can borrow it. A farm of clones needs a tenth distinct commons with a real catchment, and the exchanged minutes show one operator holding many, so honest villages refuse.
